task.description: Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0380: independently confirm the Task.yield/2 + Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) timeout-path mechanism in ModuleRegistry.register/1's instantiate/1, determine whether wasmex 0.15.1 (the pinned version) exposes any interruption/fuel mechanism that could bound the native Wasmtime thread during Wasmex.start_link/1, check whether PluginHandler already has a cheaper interim mitigation for the same problem class, and recommend a WF-03 disposition given no tenant-facing exploit path exists today.
acceptance_criteria: register/1's timeout mechanism independently re-read and confirmed against source, not taken on faith from the issue text
wasmex's pinned version and actual Elixir-level API checked for epoch-interruption/fuel-metering support, with a concrete finding on whether it covers instantiation (Wasmex.start_link/1) specifically
PluginHandler and any other shipped module checked for a different existing mitigation for the same class of problem
docs/issues/ checked for a prior related finding (Step 0.5)
A clear disposition recommendation given (fix now / defer with documented rationale / other), with reasoning, so ORCH can decide routing

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/ for wasm-related entries. Three found besides ISS-0380 itself: ISS-0377 (Windows .so/.dll test-path issue, unrelated mechanism), ISS-0287 (Postgres pool exhaustion, unrelated), and ISS-0352 (RESOLVED, MAJOR) -- directly on point. ISS-0352 is the SAME underlying mechanism class (a genuinely-hung wasmex NIF call permanently leaks a native Wasmtime/Tokio worker thread that no BEAM-side mechanism can reclaim), discovered via REQ-170's design session and then reproduced for real in CI (hang tests in call_timeout_test.exs/plugin_handler_test.exs, not module_registry.ex). ISS-0352's own resolution is precedent-setting for this decision: ORCH did NOT attempt to fix the native-thread-doesn't-die problem itself. Instead it tagged every genuinely-hanging test with @tag :wasm_hang, excluded that tag from the default suite (test/test_helper.exs), and made lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex run those hang tests in a second, isolated, short-lived BEAM subprocess whose leaks die with the process. ISS-0352's resolution text states explicitly: 'does NOT eliminate the underlying mechanism... nothing prevents a future WASM test file... from tipping the same pool into exhaustion again' -- i.e. this codebase has already, once, deliberately chosen containment over root-fixing this exact native-thread-leak class. This is not a recurrence of ISS-0352 (different call site, different trigger -- test-suite-triggered leaks under a shared Tokio pool vs. a single ad-hoc register/1 call under a malicious/pathological input), so no severity escalation, but it is strong precedent for disposition.

STEP 1 (diagnose):

1. Confirmed mechanism by reading lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry.ex lines 220-251 (instantiate/1) directly: Wasmex.start_link/1 runs inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 under ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor; the outcome is read via Task.yield(task, @instantiation_timeout_ms) with @instantiation_timeout_ms = 5_000 (line 129); on `nil` (timeout), line 248 calls Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) then returns {:error, {:instantiation_failed, {:timeout, 5000}}}. This exactly matches ISS-0380's description -- Task.shutdown/2 is an Erlang-process-level operation (kills the Elixir Task process) and has no reach into the native Rust/Wasmtime execution the NIF call kicked off inside a BEAM dirty-NIF scheduler thread; that thread keeps running the guest's infinite loop until it either finishes or the whole BEAM node exits. Confirmed independently from source, not just re-stated from the issue text.

2. wasmex capability check: mix.lock pins wasmex 0.15.1 (hex, deps/wasmex present and readable). Read deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/engine_config.ex, store_or_caller.ex, wasmex.ex, instance.ex, and CHANGELOG.md directly (not from memory/hex docs, since the vendored source is present). Findings:
   (a) wasmex 0.15.1 DOES expose fuel metering at the Elixir level: Wasmex.EngineConfig.consume_fuel/2 (defaults false) plus Wasmex.StoreOrCaller.set_fuel/2 and get_fuel/1 -- 'when fuel runs out a trap is raised.'
   (b) wasmex 0.15.1 DOES expose a cooperative epoch-based interruption mechanism, per CHANGELOG.md: 'Added cooperative epoch-based yielding for core WebAssembly calls. Timed-out core calls are interrupted so their Store can process subsequent work.' This is realized as Wasmex.call_function/4's own timeout argument (deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex.ex ~line 414 and instance.ex ~line 147): 'If a call times out, Wasmex interrupts the WebAssembly call, discards its result, and releases the Store for subsequent operations' -- i.e. call_function's timeout is a REAL interruption of in-flight Wasm execution, not merely an Elixir-level GenServer.call timeout that abandons the caller while the guest keeps running.
   (c) CRITICAL SCOPE LIMIT: both (a) and (b) are documented and implemented ONLY around call_function (invoking an already-instantiated module's export) -- not around Wasmex.start_link/1 (instantiation itself, i.e. running the module's start/init code, which is exactly what hangs in ISS-0380's WAT fixture and in ModuleRegistry.register/1's stage 2). Wasmex.start_link/1's own @spec and options (lib/wasmex.ex line ~220) accept no timeout, fuel, or epoch option at all. So even with the pinned wasmex version's real interruption capability, there is currently NO exposed Elixir-level way to bound or interrupt a hang inside start_link/instantiation specifically -- only inside a post-instantiation call_function. ISS-0380's own claim that the real fix 'if wasmex exposes it' is uncertain -- CONFIRMED as accurate and CONFIRMED as currently NOT exposed for the instantiation path, only for the call path. A genuine fix would need either (i) an upstream wasmex feature/version bump adding an interruptible/timed instantiation, or (ii) restructuring to defer all correctness-sensitive work into a call_function-shaped call, or (iii) a fuel budget set on the Store BEFORE start_link if guest start-function fuel consumption is honored during instantiation (unverified here -- would require an experiment: set_fuel before start_link and confirm whether the trap actually fires during instantiation, not just during call_function). Recording as an open question for whichever future requirement takes this on, not resolving it here (would require live experimentation against a hang fixture, which is exactly the class of experiment this project's own TEST-DESIGNER already declined to leave in CI for ISS-0380, per the issue's own text).

3. Existing interim-mitigation check: lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex's moduledoc (lines 41-56, 'Residual risk -- NOT covered by the process boundary') already discloses the IDENTICAL class of gap for its own call path: 'a Wasmtime- or NIF-layer crash... does not raise, exit, or trap in the ordinary BEAM sense... The process boundary this module relies on... bounds hangs and guest traps... it does not bound a native crash. This is an accepted, stated limitation, not a gap this module papers over.' PluginHandler's own run_guest/3 (lines 147-171) uses the SAME pattern as ModuleRegistry -- Task.Supervisor.async_nolink + Task.yield + Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) at the outer PluginInterface.invoke/2,3 layer -- and its moduledoc explicitly states an uncaught timeout/shutdown 'can... orphan that one instance -- pre-existing, disclosed behavior (REQ-165/170), not a change here.' So PluginHandler does NOT have a materially different or cheaper mitigation for the native-thread-survival problem; it has the SAME mitigation (Elixir-level task supervision bounding hangs/traps, explicitly NOT bounding native-level survival) and the SAME accepted-limitation disclosure pattern ISS-0380 is proposing for ModuleRegistry. This is corroborating precedent, not an alternative fix to borrow.

RECOMMENDATION: (b) -- defer, documented, not fixed now. Reasoning: (i) ISS-0380's own text already correctly scopes the real fix to a future tenant-facing-path requirement, and my independent wasmex API check confirms that scoping is accurate -- the pinned wasmex version's real interruption/fuel capabilities do not currently cover the instantiation path this bug is in, so there is no concretely-actionable, safely-testable code fix available today without either an upstream version bump/feature check or a live-hang experiment that (per the issue's own stated reasoning, which I agree with) should not be committed as an automated regression test. (ii) This codebase has direct, recent precedent (ISS-0352) for choosing structural containment over root-fixing this exact class of native-thread-leak problem when the blast radius is bounded, and separate direct precedent (PluginHandler's moduledoc) for disclosing this exact class of gap as an accepted, stated limitation at the call site rather than solving it preemptively. (iii) No tenant-facing exploit path exists today (independently confirmed via grep: ModuleRegistry.register/1's only application-code caller is Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry (REQ-173, lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_version_registry.ex line 269), and ModuleVersionRegistry itself has no application-code caller anywhere in lib/ outside its own module and a moduledoc cross-reference in plugin_handler.ex -- i.e. the call chain that would eventually reach register/1 with attacker-controlled bytes exists in code but is not wired to any HTTP route, GenServer boundary, or other tenant-reachable entry point yet; only tests call ModuleVersionRegistry's registration functions today). Recommended concrete action for whichever agent (ELIXIR-DEV directly, or via a lighter non-full-pipeline path per CLAUDE.md's ORCH sizing rule -- ORCH's call, not mine): add a code comment at module_registry.ex's instantiate/1 timeout branch (around line 247-249) and a short moduledoc note (near the existing 'Two-stage validation gate' section) cross-referencing ISS-0380 by id, stating plainly that Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) does not stop the underlying native Wasmtime execution thread, that wasmex 0.15.1 exposes epoch-interruption/fuel metering ONLY for call_function (not start_link/instantiation), and that this must be revisited by whichever requirement first exposes a tenant-facing WASM module-registration path -- mirroring PluginHandler's own existing 'Residual risk' moduledoc section pattern almost verbatim so a future implementer cannot miss it. This is a doc/comment-only change touching no runtime behavior, no tests, and no security-relevant code path, so it plausibly qualifies for ORCH's direct-action sizing rule (CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md §10) rather than the full CODE-DESIGNER->...->TEST-RUNNER chain -- but that determination and any routing decision is explicitly left to ORCH, not made unilaterally here.

ISS-0380.yaml's status is left as 'open' (not resolved) since no code change was made in this step; ORCH should decide whether the recommended doc-only change (once applied) is sufficient to close it, or whether it should remain open pending the future tenant-facing-path requirement.
result.next_action: ORCH decides disposition: recommended path is (b) documented-not-fixed (moduledoc/comment cross-reference at module_registry.ex's instantiate/1 timeout branch, mirroring plugin_handler.ex's existing 'Residual risk' section) rather than routing to CODE-DESIGNER for a full fix design, given wasmex 0.15.1 has no interruption/fuel mechanism exposed for Wasmex.start_link/1 (instantiation), no tenant-facing exploit path exists today, and direct codebase precedent (ISS-0352, plugin_handler.ex moduledoc) exists for containment/disclosure over root-fixing this exact native-thread-leak class. If ORCH agrees, this may be small enough for ORCH's own direct-action sizing rule (CLAUDE.md / ORCHESTRATOR.md §10) rather than the full WF-03 fix chain; if ORCH disagrees and wants the real fix attempted, route to CODE-DESIGNER with this handoff's wasmex-capability findings (section 2 above) as required reading.
